written.myAnswer: Ionic bonds usually form between metal and non-metal atoms.
An ionic bond forms when electrons transfer from one atom to another, producing oppositely charged ions. Their electrostatic attraction holds them together.
Covalent bonds form between non-metal atoms.
A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pair(s); an ionic bond forms when electron(s) transfer from one atom to another, producing oppositely charged ions.
Metal layers can slide over one another while the metallic bonding continues to hold the structure together.
Yes. A coordinate covalent bond is a strong covalent bond once formed.
An ionic bond forms by transfer of electron(s), producing oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction. A covalent bond forms when bonded atoms share an electron pair.
In the three-dimensional NaCl crystal lattice, each Na⁺ ion is surrounded by Cl⁻ ions and each Cl⁻ ion by Na⁺ ions; each ion has six nearest neighbours of opposite charge.

Ionic compounds generally have high melting and boiling points, are often soluble in water, and conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water. Covalent compounds generally have lower melting and boiling points, often do not dissolve in water, and do not conduct electricity.
In Al₂Cl₆, two chlorine atoms act as bridges between the AlCl₃ units. Each donates a lone pair to the electron-deficient aluminium atom of the other unit, forming two coordinate covalent bonds.
